definitions.explanation: A natural or man-made channel through which water flows. Includes irrigation channels, drainage ditches, canals, and navigable waterways.

examples.japanese: {水路|すいろ}に{沿|そ}って{歩|ある}いた。
{農業|のうぎょう}{用|よう}の{水路|すいろ}が{田|た}んぼに{水|みず}を{供給|きょうきゅう}している。
examples.english: Agricultural waterways supply water to the rice paddies.

examples.japanese: この{街|まち}には{江戸時代|えどじだい}に{造|つく}られた{水路|すいろ}が{今|いま}も{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: Waterways built in the Edo period still remain in this town.

notes:
USAGE:
{水路|すいろ} is a general term covering both natural and artificial water channels. Compare with {運河|うんが} (canal), which specifically refers to large man-made waterways for navigation or transport, and {用水路|ようすいろ} (irrigation channel), which is specifically for agricultural water supply. {水路|すいろ} can refer to any of these.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水路|すいろ}を{開|ひら}く: to open a waterway
- {水路|すいろ}を{整備|せいび}する: to maintain waterways
- {農業|のうぎょう}{用|よう}{水路|すいろ}: agricultural waterway
- {水路|すいろ}{図|ず}: nautical chart
